packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-25 -- first reader response (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. The filename of the reader prompt and the packet path mention "stams-c5ugo-batch-8"; the images themselves carry pencil shelfmark notes reading "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-1r / 1v / 2r / 2v" (visible on the leaves). No work/author identification was seen.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only, from overviews image-001 and image-017)

image-001 (overview, face A): two leaves laid side by side on black ground, colour checker lower left, ruler right.
 - Left leaf pencilled "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-2r"; right leaf "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-1r".
 - Both leaves are very faded/abraded on this face. Much of what is visible appears to be show-through (mirror-image) of the other side: the large display word at top of the left leaf is seen in reverse (the heading of 2v showing through). Ruled horizontal lines are visible throughout; ink of this face is extremely faint, with darker patches of cursive near lower left of 2r (lines around the tear) and lower half of 1r.
 - Each leaf has folded/ cut strips (left leaf: narrow strip at right edge; right leaf: tapering strip at left edge and strip at foot) -- binding-waste trimming. A long tear at lower left of 2r.
 - Single column, long lines, apparently a German-language cursive (Kurrent-type) document hand rather than a book hand. Single column of roughly 35-40 lines per leaf (estimate).

image-017 (overview, face B): the other side of the same two leaves.
 - Left leaf pencilled "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-2v"; right leaf "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-1v".
 - 2v: large brown display word at top left (heading, enlarged textura/fraktur-like letters, read tentatively "...rlannder" / "Erlannder"?), then a single column of densely written cursive, ca. 40 lines, plus a narrow strip at left (folded margin) also carrying line-ends/line-beginnings of text. Lower part has a tear and damage; a few lines near foot, then blank ruled space.
 - 1v: single column of cursive text from top to ca. 3/4 down, with some short lines (paragraph ends / headings such as a line beginning "Fryl." or similar at left, about line 7), last lines lower; a signature-like word lower right ("Joha..?"). Strip at right edge carries more text.
 - Interpretation (tentative): a German-language administrative/legal or account document (paper or parchment) in a 15th/16th-century cursive, reused as binding waste. Not a glossed book layout; no columns, no rubrics other than the 2v heading.

Plan: face B (image-017, tiles 018-037, 5 columns x 4 rows) is the more legible; I read it first, then face A (image-001, tiles 002-016, 5 x 3) as far as images allow.
Tile map assumption (face B): row1 = 018-022, row2 = 023-027, row3 = 028-032, row4 = 033-037, left to right across the whole overview (so 018/023/028/033 cover left part of 2v incl. strip; 021-022 etc. cover 1v).

TRANSCRIPTIONS

Method note: tiles are very faint. For each tile I view a grayscale, auto-contrast + contrast x1.8 derivative of the whole tile (saved as rscratch/packet-25/enh-NNN.jpg), which is a processed copy of the named image file, not a different source. For tile 018 I also viewed the original and one enhanced crop (rscratch/packet-25/018-enh.jpg).

--- image-018 (face B, top-left: leaf 2v, heading + start of lines; left strip) ---
Heading (large brown display script, first letter lost at torn edge):
018 H: [.]rlannde[r]   (the visible letters "rlannde" then cut; overview shows final "r": "...rlannder")
Main column (left part of lines only; line ends continue in image-019). Line numbers from top of image:
018 l1: [..]nd del? Stamm der hohen/ D[...]      ("Stamm" or "Stamen"; reading "des/del" uncertain)
018 l2: [..]en vnd bewilligung vß? ber[...]
018 l3: [..]endt/ als Innamen? des[...]   ("als Inmassen?" also possible; uncertain)
018 l4: [A?]bschrifftlichen? Zuegestelt[...]
018 l5: [..]ain Bezalung? ain gros[...]   (word after "ain" uncertain: Be?a?nsung)
018 l6: [..]en Brieffen? [illegible] [...]
018 l7: [..]endten? [illegible; ink blot] [...]
Left folded strip: only faint line-ends of a previous/adjacent text block visible ("..ff", "..er"); not legible.

--- image-019 (face B, top row, 2nd tile: top margin of 2v) ---
Viewed only in a failed (over-stretched) enhancement; showed: end of heading "...nder" in large brown display letters (overlaps 018 heading: so heading = "[.]rlannder"); pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-2v"; first text lines washed out, only "vnd? ... Ben[...]" glimpsed near the right. No reliable reading; NOT re-viewed (image budget). Lines 1-3 of 2v right of the 018 portion remain unread.

--- image-023 (face B, row 2, left: 2v lines ca. 4-20, left part; plus folded left strip) ---
Overlap: l1-l3 = 018 l4-l6.
Main column, left portion (strip text at far left given in [strip: ]):
023 l1: [..]berschickhen? zuegestelt[...]   (= 018 l4)
023 l2: [..]ain Bezansung? ain gros[...]   (= 018 l5)
023 l3: [..]en Briefen? [ink blot] [...]   (= 018 l6)
023 l4: [strip: ..sthof?] [..]wunschten? fragen[?] [blot] [...]
023 l5: [strip: Oberen?] [..]enfacung? sein/ als we[...]
023 l6: [strip: vnd das] [..] den hoch?[...]   (word after "den" a long word beginning h-, possibly "hochkhunfft"? uncertain)
023 l7: [strip: alten?] [..]ben vnnder? [...]
023 l8: [strip: ..halten] [..]aufs? fleissigst? Ihr? [...]
023 l9: [strip: ..] [..] sonnderlich vnd [...]
023 l10: [strip: ..gert?] [..]allain? Weiß? [...]
023 l11: [strip: ..khomen?] [..] noch? [..] tail? [...]
023 l12: [strip: ..sel selbs?] [..] , [erasure/blank oval] Wann aber[...]
023 l13: [..]gen? [..]vngefangen?/ vnnd [...]
023 l14: [..] ist? [..] solchen[...]
023 l15: [..] M? [..] verderblichen? [...]
023 l16: [..]fürderlich?/ ...[illegible]
Confidence: low throughout; hand is a rapid German chancery/Kurrent cursive with looped ascenders; letters e/n/m/u minims hard to separate in this light. A tear/fold runs vertically at the strip boundary.

--- image-020 (face B, top row, middle: right edge of 2v lines 1-10 at left; start of leaf 1v lines 1-10 at right) ---
Left part (2v, line-ends only, heavy blot lower centre): mostly illegible ends: l1 "...Ve? gegen? Wa[...]", l3 "...sachen?", l5 "...gefangen?" -- all very uncertain; not usable.
Right part = leaf 1v, beginnings of lines (left margin of 1v at ca. x=740; first letters partly in damaged edge):
020 l1: [..]ssig?/ Von Doctorn? f[...]    (a tall cross-like/T-like ascender over "Von"; possibly an abbreviation stroke)
020 l2: [..]n gegenwurt? Ihr? [...]
020 l3: [..]n ..haimisch? abt? / ...[...]   ("Hainvsen" or "haimsen" -- uncertain)
020 l4: [..] vnd? [..]ten? andern? [...]
020 l5: [..]und gerechtigkhait?, da[...]
020 l6: [..]mer/ ain hochzeit?/ an[...]   ("ain sachen"? "hochzeit" uncertain)
020 l7: [..]ren? glegen?/ allain [...]
020 l8: [..] Kost?. Wetter? Va[...]   (short sense break: point after first word; overview suggests a new item begins here, "Fryl./Kost." uncertain)
020 l9: [..]die Gnaden?/ Ca?[...]
020 l10: [..]? [illegible]

--- image-021 (face B, top row, 4th: 1v lines 1-11, middle portion; pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 10-1[v]") ---
Overlap: line starts at left edge continue 020 l1-l10. Surface extremely faint/abraded; most of the tile illegible even enhanced.
021 l1: [..]sammen? hab? [illegible] [...]
021 l2-l4: [illegible] (only "ab", "ff" strokes)
021 l5: [..]ch?, das? g[...] [illegible]
021 l6: [..]em, ain? [illegible] ...
021 l7: [..]bein? [illegible] ... (dense, illegible)
021 l8: [illegible] ... Wll? [illegible]
021 l9: [..] Ca? [..] [illegible] abschid? verplibt? [...]   (word "Abschid/Abschied" uncertain)
021 l10: [illegible]
Note: not a gap of effort; ink here is almost entirely lost.

--- image-022 (face B, top row, right: right end of 1v lines 1-12 and the folded right strip) ---
Pencil shelfmark "...Frg. 10-1v" (final letter looks like r or v in this view). Ink blot ca. line 5. Text extremely faint:
022 l7: [...]wandlet?/ [..]
022 l9: [...]ent? [..] ad[...]
022 l11: [...]Obr? Herrn? [..]
Right strip (separate piece/fold, text continues line-ends of 1v or belongs to an adjacent layer): only "...yer? ..." "...vnd? ..." faint. Illegible otherwise.

--- image-024 (face B, row 2, 2nd: 2v, middle of lines ca. 4-19) ---
Overlap: left edge continues 023 lines (023 l2 "...ain gros" ends at 024 l1 left). Show-through from the other side crosses the writing, and a dark stain lower centre. Readings very tentative:
024 l1: [..]ain gros[..] [illegible] ...hochgef?[...]
024 l2: [..] [illegible; looped "R?"/"Q?" capital] [...]
024 l3: [..]n vnverschafft? hab? [..] [illegible] [...]
024 l4: [..]als vnmüglich? Zeit? [..] g[..]n? [...]
024 l5: [..]ꝯ? haben? / 1. ich? da? [...]   (possible numeral "1." or abbreviation; uncertain)
024 l6: [..] [illegible] mand? halten? [...]
024 l7: [..] [illegible] vergebenlich? [...]
024 l8: [..]vnd? [..] ding? [...]
024 l11: [..] aber? [..] [illegible] [..] , we?[...]
024 l12-l16: [illegible] (stain; scattered "solchen?", "vnd")
No connected span reliable on this tile.

--- image-025 (face B, row 2, middle: left = right ends of 2v lines ca. 9-25; right = beginnings of 1v lines ca. 7-22) ---
Overlap: right half l1-l3 = 020 l7-l9.
Left part (2v line-ends): mostly illegible; "...gefangen?", "...lassen?", "...hab?" glimpsed; not usable.
Right part (1v, line beginnings):
025 r1: [..]ren glegen?/ [...]                 (= 020 l7)
025 r2: [..] Kost?. Wetter? Va[...]             (= 020 l8)
025 r3: [..]die Gegnen?/ Cai?[...]             (= 020 l9)
025 r4: [..]Bre? eifern?/ G(naden?) [..]n[...]  (looped capital G with loop, maybe "Gn" abbreviation)
025 r5: [..]n solches die verzug?[...]
025 r6: [..]n Ich abgemelt[en?] [...]
025 r7: [..]gnn? [..]mögen?/ [..] [...]
025 r8: [..]ung? abgemelt[..] [...]
025 r9: [..]rung? mit? zue [...]
025 r10: [..] vnd G(naden?)/ [..]n Ju?[...]
025 r11: [..] [illegible] Ja?[...]
025 r12: [..]hin? thail?, [..]so? [...]
025 r13: bewilligen? ge[...]
025 r14: [..]parole? komen? a[...]   (second word perhaps "komen"; first uncertain)
025 r15: [..]ellen genugsam?[...]
025 r16: [..]? alle? ... [...]

=== SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS ===
- Object: two leaves (pencilled Stams, StA, Frg. 10-1 and 10-2, recto/verso) of a German-language cursive document, frame-ruled, reused as binding waste (turned-in strips at edges). Single column of long lines.
- Face B (1v, 2v) carries the only readable text. 2v opens with a large brown display word "[.]rlannder" (first letter lost), and the first text line continues on the same line after a comma ("..., auf dem ..."). Most secure words on 2v: "Stamm der hohen", "bewilligung", "zuegestelt", "ain gros", "bezallen", "Wann aber", "sonnderlich vnd", "verderblichen?". On 1v: "abgemelt(en)" (twice), "gerechtigkhait?", "Ich abgemelten", "solches die verzug?", "Land-", "Sigl?", "Johan?".
- Face A (1r, 2r) main text is almost entirely faded; what shows is mostly show-through from face B (the 2v heading appears in mirror at the top of 2r). One darker later line on lower 2r: "[..]nn? [..] Lehs? vom yezt? Kaiß? kauff[..]m?" (uncertain), with short words below.
- Mirror-image dark lines on face B tiles 029/031/034/036 are show-through of darker lines on 2r/1r, not text of 2v/1v.
- Readings are low-confidence throughout because of fading and two-sided show-through; nearly every word carries "?". No connected span of 10+ secure lines was achievable on any face; the best continuous spans are 2v lines 1-6 (018+019) and 1v line beginnings 7-16 (020/025).
- Selected areas: 2v top (018/019/023), 2v lower-left (028/029), 1v left line-beginnings (020/025/030), 1v right line-ends (032/037), 2r dark lower line (012/013). Unread/illegible: 2v right-hand line ends (020 left, 025 left, 030 left), most of 1v middle (021, 026, 031), and essentially all of face A.
- Suggested: multispectral/UV imaging would be needed for face A; a raking-light or UV view of face B 2v lines 1-25 would help most.
- Beyond the rules: I viewed processed derivatives (grayscale, contrast-stretched copies) of every tile instead of the raw tiles (raw viewed only for 018 and overviews), plus one enhanced crop of 018; all saved in rscratch/packet-25/.
